France. A major European nation in Western Europe whose cultural, political, and artistic influence on the world has been immense since the medieval period. From the seat of absolute monarchy at Versailles to the radical ideals of the Revolution, from the military conquests of Napoleon to its role in world wars and the modern European Union, France has repeatedly reshaped European civilization.

Under Louis the Fourteenth, the Sun King, who reigned from sixteen forty-three to seventeen fifteen, France became the dominant European power and the model of absolute monarchy. Versailles symbolized royal grandeur. The French Revolution from seventeen eighty-nine to seventeen ninety-nine overthrew the monarchy and introduced revolutionary ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity, triggering decades of European conflict. Napoleon Bonaparte rose from the Revolution's chaos to conquer much of Europe. Though defeated, he permanently altered the political map and legal systems of Europe.

France's classical culture—literature, philosophy, and art—shaped the Enlightenment. Figures like Voltaire, Rousseau, and Descartes defined European thought. The Louvre in Paris, originally a royal palace, became the world's greatest art museum, housing masterworks like the Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo. French Romanticism and later Impressionism through artists like Monet, Renoir, and Degas revolutionized visual art and established Paris as the artistic capital of the world in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

France was a central battleground and power in both World Wars. The Vichy regime's collaboration with Nazi Germany and the subsequent liberation shaped modern French identity. The Enlightenment was an intellectual movement centered in Paris that transformed Western thought. Victor Hugo was a great French Romantic novelist whose work defined the era. Impressionism was the revolutionary art movement that emerged in Paris in the late nineteenth century. Gothic architecture was exemplified in French cathedrals like Chartres and Notre-Dame. Charlemagne was a Frankish emperor who founded an early European empire centered on what became France.
